Explanation: Algorithms learn from labeled training data to predict outcomes for unseen data (e.g., Linear Regression, Random Forests, Neural Networks).
Discovers hidden patterns or data groupings without human guidance or pre-existing labels (e.g., K-Means, PCA, Hierarchical Clustering).
Overfitting occurs when a model learns training data noise and fails to generalize (high variance). Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture trends (high bias).
Optimization algorithm used to minimize the loss function by iteratively moving in the direction of steepest descent determined by the negative gradient.
Core algorithm for training neural networks. Uses the chain rule of calculus to compute loss gradients with respect to each weight and bias in reverse order.
Deep learning architecture using convolutional kernels and pooling layers, highly effective for image processing and spatial pattern recognition.
Architecture based on Self-Attention mechanisms that eliminates recurrence, enabling massive parallelization for NLP and vision models like BERT and GPT.
